title: Yankees' Carlos Rodon strikes out seven in potential final rehab start
description: Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodon followed up a strong first rehab start with a gem on Thursday night, pitching 4.1 scoreless innings and striking out seven batters for Double-A Somerset.
fullText:
Carlos Rodon followed up a strong first rehab start with a gem on Thursday night.

Pitching for Double-A Somerset, the Yankees southpaw tossed 4.1 shutout innings and allowed two hits and one walk while striking out seven batters.

After a delayed start due to inclement weather, Rodon took the mound and allowed a bloop single to lead off the game. Rodon bounced back, getting a fly out and an inning-ending double play to end the first frame.

Rodon then came out in the second, striking out two in a 1-2-3 inning. After Somerset put up a four-spot in the bottom half of the second, Rodon worked around a leadoff single by striking out the next three batters to keep New Hampshire off the board. Rodon struck out two more batters in the fourth before issuing his first walk to lead off the fifth inning. After picking up an out, Rodon was pulled in the middle of an at-bat after 58 pitches (41 strikes).

Tyler Boudreau came in to finish up the at-bat Rodon left for and got the third out without allowing Rodon's runner to score, putting an end to the veteran's night.

In his last rehab start, Rodon struck out four batters while allowing three runs on three hits and two walks across 2.2 innings. Thursday's start was a stark improvement as Rodon continues to build up his pitch count.

Earlier this week, Yankees manager Aaron Boone said this could be Rodon's final rehab start before rejoining the team. If Rodon feels good after Thursday's start, he can be activated next week, even with the limited pitch count. Boone actually stated that Rodon could continue to build up his count while pitching in a piggyback situation.

That could be a temporary solution for the upcoming rotation crunch that will befall the Yankees. When Rodon is ready to start games, New York will have to decide which of Will Warren or Ryan Weathers will be added to the bullpen.

title: Thanks to Yankees teammate, Jasson Dominguez made a change that could unleash Martian
description: A week after being demoted by the Yankees to Triple-A, Jasson Dominguez met up with NJ.com before a game this week in Allentown, Pennsylvania.
fullText:
ALLENTOWN, Pa. — Jasson Dominguez used to think that he was one of the hardest workers on his teams, and why not?

He always showed up on time. He always gave an honest effort. He never took shortcuts. He never got big-headed when the Yankees gave him a $5.1 million signing bonus at age 16 or when he was being compared to all-time greats before he played his first game as a professional.

Whether Dominguez was in the minors or was with the Yankees, he always cared about improving in all parts of his game, especially his fielding.

An American League scout who has watched Dominguez since he was playing Low-A ball in Tampa agreed.

"He never dogged it," the scout told NJ.com recently. "He worked hard. But he never was the hardest worker on his club. There was always someone next to him on the field giving more effort. It was noticeable that Dominguez wasn't going above and beyond to get better when others around him with half his talent were."

When that assessment was shared with Dominguez on Tuesday night before he played left field for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders, he responded with a smile and a nod.

"Oh, definitely," Dominguez said. "For sure. I've always worked hard, but definitely now I'm working more than what I used to do. That's from being in the big leagues and having great teammates."

Dominguez's work habits began changing late last season. When the Yankees upgraded their bench by trading for Amed Rosario, the hard-working journeyman infielder took Dominguez, a fellow Dominican, under his wing.

"Rosario is the guy that pushed me," Dominguez said. "He's a guy that literally came early every day to do his work and I started doing that with him."

When Rosario re-signed with the Yankees last winter, he pushed Dominguez during their spring training workouts on and off the field. Dominguez maintained a hard-working mentality when he started this season in the minors through his time with the Yankees, which also featured a stint on the injured list for a shoulder injury.

Rosario and Dominguez were separated again on Aug. 3, when the Yankees acquired outfielder Heliot Ramos at the trade deadline and rookie Spencer Jones was picked over Dominguez to remain in the majors.

Back with Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, Dominguez no longer needs anyone to motivate him.

"I felt pretty good with Rosario around and now I keep doing it because I understand that I've got things that I need to improve," Dominguez said. "I understand what needs to be done now. It's working harder than I ever worked, trying to get better and hopefully get back up to the big leagues."

Dominguez has been improving. In his first few years as a professional, Dominguez was so much better as a left-handed hitter that some scouts suggested that he give up batting right-handed. This year, he's been better as a right-handed hitter.

His outfield play is still below average, but his minus-1 Outs Above Average ranking in Baseball Savant's metrics is much better than last season's worst-in-the-league minus-9.

"I see a player who's constantly getting better, and that's the most important thing," RailRiders manager Shelley Duncan said. "Jasson has been in the spotlight a lot, and when you make mistakes with fundamentals or make mental errors in New York, it gets highlighted more than anywhere else in all of baseball.

"If you like take a guy like Jasson and that stuff happened in other places, it might slide under the radar and not even get noticed and you just chalk it up as a young guy learning. I say that because all of the mistakes that Jasson's made over his career, he learned from them and I've seen him grow as a player."

Dominguez will tell you that he's not close to his prime. He wants to live up to his Martian nickname and comparisons from his teenage years to Yankees legend Mickey Mantle and present-day superstar Mike Trout. That's a far-fetched dream, but he still has time to develop into an All-Star.

"I hope one day I can meet those reputations for sure, but at the end of the day, Mike Trout is Mike Trout and Mickey Mantle is Mickey Mantle," Dominguez said. "They've already done it. I'm trying to grow myself to be able to do it, too."

His opening act as a big leaguer featured a first-inning homer in his first game in Houston off future Hall of Famer Justin Verlander. He was 20 on Sept. 1, 2023. A few days later, he was headed for Tommy John surgery.

Almost three years later, he's been a mixed bag of highs, lows and more injuries. He's a career .243 hitter with 22 homers, 72 RBI, 36 steals and a .703 OPS in 741 plate appearances over 202 games.

In 2025, Dominguez batted .257 with 10 homers and 47 RBI in 123 games, but his fielding woes led to virtually no playing time in the final two months before he was sent back to Triple-A to open 2026.

He's crushed it in Triple-A this year, hitting .313 with six homers and 21 RBI in 33 games, but his numbers in 53 games with the Yankees were disappointing — .230 with six homers and 14 RBI in 53 games, most of them filling in right field for injured three-time MVP Aaron Judge.

"Jasson has what it takes to be really good," Scranton bench coach Gil Velazquez said. "He's disciplined. He's a good baseball player, period. He's still young and it takes a good amount of reps to be able to not get surprised with situations and not make dumb mistakes. Everybody goes through that."

Dominguez is still going through it. In his last full series, he misplayed a couple of balls in the right field corner at Wrigley Field. These were unforced mistakes in his mind, and they upset him.

"I want to improve the mental side," he said. "I have to make better decisions. That's one thing that I need to get better at."

That's part of the reason Dominguez is back in the minors.

After being optioned, he spent the allotted 72 hours he had to report to Triple-A at his New Jersey home with his family.

"I used those three days to reset my mind so I could go to Scranton with the best attitude," he said. "Obviously, I want to be in the big leagues, but it is what it is now. If I came down here with a bad attitude and pouted or whatever, that's not gonna help me get back up."

Dominguez trusts the Yankees are doing what's best for his career. He's focused.

"I want to improve my whole game," he said.

Slowly but surely, it's growing.

"He cut a ball down in the left-field corner and threw a runner out at second the other day," Duncan bragged. "His decision making and throwing is a lot better in the outfield this year. His focus pitch to pitch has gotten better every time I've seen him.

"It's fun watching Jasson hit because he's a carefree-loose type of hitter that can hit any type of pitcher. Those are fun hitters to have. He's got the talent and skillset to be a really good big leaguer for a long time."

title: Yankees At-Bat of the Week: George Lombard Jr. (8/8)
description: Lombard’s leadoff home run in the seventh inning against the Braves on Saturday turned out to be the game winner.
fullText:
I don't want to spill too much ink on the sorry state of the Yankees offense at the risk of sounding like a broken record. Instead, let's focus on the positives they have provided us in recent days, namely an improbable series win over the Braves. As much as the pitching largely carried the day, a certain young shortstop provided a handful of bright sparks on either side of the ball, and so George Lombard Jr. earns his first appearance on At-bat of the Week.

We join Lombard leading off the bottom of the seventh of the middle game against the Braves on Saturday. The Yankees are clinging to a 3-2 lead courtesy of a Spencer Jones RBI single in the second and RBI triple in the fifth, Austin Wells then driving him home with a double. Lombard enters this AB having struck out and drawn a walk against Chris Sale, the latter result requiring a pair of impressive, successful ABS challenges. However, Lombard now faces the hard-throwing righty reliever Victor Mederos, a very different look from the sidearming southpaw Sale.

Mederos starts Lombard with a first pitch sinker at 96 looking to tie the hitter up on the inner half.

This is a really good take from Lombard. The sinker looks like a strike on the upper ledge of the strike zone for much of its path toward home. It exits Mederos' hand aimed pretty centrally, yet Lombard is able to diagnose it immediately as a fastball and understands that the foot-and-a-half of arm side run will carry it all the way off the plate and out of the zone inside for a ball.

That was a pretty good pitch that Mederos just threw, so it makes sense that he sticks with the inside sinker as it's a pitch that can really eat up a hitter when buried in on the hands.

This is exactly why we don't bunt unless it is absolutely necessary. When you've got a reliever coming in and throwing upper-90s, a middle-middle sinker in a 1-0 count might be the best pitch you're gonna get to hit. Not only did Lombard miss a golden pitch to hit, but he lost his count leverage without making the pitcher work for it. Yes, I understand the third baseman was playing back and the Yankees are struggling for base runners at the moment, but Lombard was brought up to swing the bat (and for his glove) and bunting in this spot amounted to giving away a pitch.

Now that Mederos has shown Lombard a pair of fastballs that break toward him, he switches to a cutter breaking away from the batter, hoping he can get him to chase something off the plate outside should he mistakenly assume it is another sinker breaking in.

Mederos yanks this pitch way out of the zone, the pitch passing through the lefty batter's box and off the catcher's mitt to the backstop. It's one of the easier takes Lombard will get, though it was still informative for him to see a fastball that breaks in the opposite direction from the first two he saw.

After missing so wildly with that cutter, Mederos breaks out his third different fastball of the encounter, the four-seamer. His four-seamer breaks a little less down and a little less arm-side than his sinker, but the two pitch types otherwise aren't all that distinguishable from each other.

Mederos nails the outside edge with this 97 mph heater. He's partially able to catch Lombard looking by sequencing this pitch directly following a fastball that breaks glove-side, this pitch starting well off the plate away before tailing back into the zone, but mostly it's just a well-executed fastball that Lombard is more than justified to watch for a called strike.

Mederos now tries to leverage that called strike on the outside edge by sequencing a cutter that, as we mentioned, moves in the opposite lateral direction as his sinker and four-seamer. Lombard just watched a pitch that looked like a ball away end up as a called strike on the outside edge, so he effectively has to protect against anything that starts aimed away. This should make him susceptible to chasing a pitch that breaks glove-side.

Instead, Mederos grooves this cutter up and out over the plate. It doesn't have any of the cut of the first one he threw and flies straight as an arrow toward home. Lombard fires a beautiful swing lining this pitch into the seats in right for a leadoff home run to give the Yankees an invaluable late insurance run that they would need by the time the final out was recorded. I'll be honest, I did not realize Lombard had opposite field home run power, short porch or not. However, I love his approach, staying behind the baseball and allowing the velocity on the pitch to supply the power off the bat, knowing that with solid contact in the air, there's always a chance to leave the yard in right.

Without getting ahead of ourselves from a five-game sample, it is all the same assuring that Lombard has not looked overmatched facing big league pitching according to the eye test. We were always told that the defense was MLB-ready and indeed Lombard already looks way more rangy and self-assured at short than Anthony Volpe. However, I was not expecting him to have such an immediate impact with the bat. The power is certainly a welcome surprise, but it's his advanced pitch recognition and plate discipline that have really caught the eye and could be the keys to maintaining this form down the stretch.

title: New York Yankees vs. Seattle Mariners: Series Preview
description: The Yankees face a trident of right-handers as the scuffling Mariners dock in the Bronx.
fullText:
After three straight series against the Senior Circuit, the Yankees welcome the Mariners to the East Coast. The Bombers had an off day on Monday after dropping the series finale against the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. The Yankees continue to hold serve as they wait for reinforcements to arrive, posting a 5-5 mark over their last 10 games, including an even 3-3 record thus far on the homestand.

The Mariners dock in New York after being swept at home by the pesky and, at this point, must-be-declared-legit Tampa Bay Rays. Seattle's season has not gone according to plan, as star catcher Cal Raleigh has struggled and the club enters play Tuesday sitting at 56-63. The Mariners have dropped four straight and are just 3-7 over their last 10 games.

This series features two night games before Thursday's getaway game, currently scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET. Let's dive into which Mariners will be manning the harpoons and which Yankees white whales will be hoping to avoid the trident.

Tuesday: Ryan Weathers vs. Bryan Woo (7:05 pm ET)

Weathers has had a bit of an up-and-down first season in the Bronx. After opening the year looking solid, the month of June was not kind to the left-hander. However, since the calendar flipped to July, Weathers has found his footing again. Weathers currently has a 5-7 record, 3.79 ERA, and a 1.22 WHIP for the season.

Over his last three starts, he has thrown 18.2 innings while allowing just one earned run. That stretch includes six scoreless innings in his most recent outing against the Cardinals at home. Weathers has had his struggles in pinstripes this season, posting a 4.11 ERA at home compared to a 3.35 ERA on the road, but he will look to keep the ball in the yard and continue building on this recent momentum.

Woo is one of the best young pitchers in baseball, featuring a dominant four-seam fastball, excellent command, and the type of arm slot and tunneling that makes pitching nerds drool. The good news? Woo has been two very different pitchers this season.

At home, he owns an ace-like 7-0 record with a 1.96 ERA. On the road, however, Woo is 1-8 with a 6.71 ERA. That difference has held true recently as well. In his last two home starts, Woo has allowed just two earned runs across 13 innings. In his last two road starts, however, he has been roughed up for 10 earned runs in 10 innings. Those splits bring his overall season numbers to 8-8 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.12 WHIP. Expect Aaron Boone to send as many left-handed hitters to the plate as possible, as Woo's platoon splits also favor the lefties. Left-handed hitters have posted a .700 OPS against Woo this season compared to .585 from righties.

Wednesday: Will Warren vs. Bryce Miller (7:00 pm ET)

Much like Weathers, Warren has had his ups and downs throughout the 2026 season. Currently sitting at 8-6 with a 4.18 ERA, Warren's season has felt a bit like a roller coaster. After starting the year in dominant fashion, he has struggled as the weather has warmed. In July, Warren went 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA.

Warren has looked better in his last two starts. Against the Cubs, he tossed 6.2 scoreless innings, and in his most recent turn against the Cardinals, he allowed three runs over 5.1 innings. As one of the backend guys in this rotation, you have to expect some turbulence with Warren, take the good with the bad, and hope he can grind his way to a quality start.

The Mariners will send another power right-hander to the mound on Wednesday, as Miller gets the ball opposite Warren. On the season, Miller sits at 4-6 with a 3.08 ERA. He features an upper-90s fastball that he pairs with a nasty splitter and sweeper. Miller primarily uses the splitter to attack lefties and the sweeper against righties, and both pitches have been effective enough to produce almost identical platoon splits. Left-handed hitters have posted a .630 OPS against Miller compared to .629 from righties.

The good news for the Yankees is that, much like Woo, Miller has struggled away from the Pacific Northwest this season. At home, he owns a 2.09 ERA, while that number balloons to 4.02 on the road. More good news? The summer months have also been less kind to Miller, who currently finds himself in his worst stretch of the season. He has not made it through the sixth inning of a start since July 2nd.

Thursday: Max Fried vs. Logan Gilbert (1:35 pm ET)

The Yankees sandwich Warren with lefties as Fried takes the ball in the series finale. Fried has been steadily building himself back up after missing about two months of the season. Since returning, he has picked up right where he left off and currently owns a 4-3 record to go along with a tidy 2.88 ERA and 0.97 WHIP.

With two August starts under his belt, Fried looks ready for the postseason push. On the first of the month, he tossed 78 pitches of one-run ball against the Cubs before reaching 90 pitches while throwing 6.1 scoreless innings against his former club, the Braves, in his most recent start. I expect the training wheels to come off soon, and might I add that having a left-handed ace take the ball every fifth day is such an awesome thing to get to watch.

While the Yankees show a little spice of life on the mound, the Mariners roll out their third straight hard-throwing righty in Gilbert for the final game. Seattle's front office clearly has a type: tall right-handers who throw hard, get extension down the mound, and command all of their offerings. It is a good type, but with no real wrinkle from one day to the next, hopefully the Yankees' bats can lock in and light up Gilbert.

Gilbert owns an 8-7 record with a 3.42 ERA and 1.00 WHIP on the season. Unlike his other companions, Gilbert has actually been better on the road this year, posting a 2.50 ERA away from home compared to a 4.01 ERA at T-Mobile Park. In his most recent start against the Rays, Gilbert went 6.2 innings and took a tough 2-1 loss after allowing a pair of solo home runs that proved to be the difference. Tampa Bay also worked four walks, a season high for Gilbert.

The Yankees took two of three when they visited Seattle back in late March and early April. Here's hoping for more of the same this time around in the Bronx.

fullText:
The Atlanta Braves are once again in a position of avoiding a sweep. The New York Yankees pulled off two low-scoring wins and are looking to accomplish a third in this finale before the Braves return home to face the team just across the city.

Grant Holmes is currently boasting a 3.77 ERA and is coming off a successful outing against the Miami Marlins just five days ago. Reestablishing his starting campaign after a shaky first half of the season, Holmes has found his command and played up to what fans were expecting coming into the season.

It's just been one game, so let's not get ahead of ourselves.

The outing, however, was a sign that Holmes still has what it takes to keep his starting spot and put on a stellar performance. He will not only have to match that showing, but top it, as it's uncertain what version of the Braves' offense will show up after their recent losses. And they need all the defense they can muster to hold the Yankees' offense.

As for New York, Cam Schlitter is set to take the start. Holding a 2.26 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and a five-pitch arsenal that's touching high velocities, it's no wonder Boston is keeping him in their conversations.

Cam Schlittler, Nasty 94mph Cutter. ✂️ pic.twitter.com/In8VOYRtW1

Though not coming off his best outing against St. Louis on August 3 with four earned runs in his three innings pitched, don't get fooled, Schlittler is a beast on the mound. And it'll take the dominant version of the Braves to stop him and avoid a sweep. They'll have to strike early with Holmes on the defensive end to continue his strong stint.

One could only hope, but the Braves will have to execute if they want this hope to turn into action.

fullText:
While the New York Yankees remain a very competitive team in the American League, they have been trying to stay afloat despite three injuries to their offensive core.

Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Cody Bellinger remain out due to injury. Despite their absence, the Yankees have found ways to win baseball games.

Throughout their last eight games, New York has gone 5-3. It isn't ideal, but the Yankees are staying afloat enough to allow their stars to get healthy. The hope is that they can return at some point down the final stretch of the regular season heading into the playoffs.

On Saturday, August 8, New York revealed a new update about Stanton. He hasn't played a game since April 24 when he went down with a calf injury.

Aaron Boone, the Yankees' manager, revealed some new details about Stanton. His latest update provides some optimism about a potential return sooner rather than later.

He stated that Stanton jogged in the outfield on Friday and "started the introduction to some bases." Boone also said that "I expect him back here at some point. He'll be in there when the time's right."

Stanton is still a very feared player at the plate when healthy. He may be 36 years old now, but he's still capable of taking baseballs out of the park.

Prior to the injury, Stanton played in just 24 games. He hit three home runs to go along with 14 RBI and a slash line of .256/.302/.422. Adding his production back into the lineup would be a big step towards legitimate World Series contention for New York.

Fans across the baseball world were quick to make their comments heard on social media.

"Unbelievable how this dude can barely move every season. Was on a massive hall of fame trajectory," one fan wrote.

Another chimed in, "Imagine being an MLB player and being introduced to touching a base again due to a strained calf."

"I can't wait for this dead weight to no longer be a Yankee. All time bad acquisition. The NTC should never happen again for any contract," a third fan commented.

Yet another fan said, "Honestly these updates are ridiculous and the whole Stanton situation is absurd."

"Have this man strap up for the Old Timers game at this point," another comment read.

Needless to say, fans are frustrated with how much time Stanton has missed. At 36, recovering from an injury gets a bit more difficult. Hopefully, more good news will be coming regarding the slugger in the near future.

title: Yankees, Braves announce new start time after rain delay
description: The Braves are in the Bronx, but so is bad weather.
fullText:
It's Unofficial 1990s Throwback Night at Yankee Stadium on Friday, as the Atlanta Braves are in town to face the Yankees for a three-game set.

These showdowns always bring to mind fond—for us anyway—memories of the 1996 and 1999 Fall Classics, when the Yankees came back from down 0-2 to win their first championship in 18 years and then when they polished off a similarly potent Braves team in a four-game sweep durig the final year of the 20th century (securing a repeat to follow the act of the legendary 1998 club). Of course, it's been many years since those rumbles, and from 2001 onward, the Yankees and Braves have the same number of titles: one apiece, in 2009 and 2021 respectively.

Tonight has a special sort of buzz about it, as erstwhile Braves ace Max Fried—who won the World Series clincher in Houston during that special 2021—will face his old team for the first time. The personnel has changed a bit since Fried departed after 2024 (including now-retired skipper Brian Snitker), but Ronald Acuña Jr., Ozzie Albies, Matt Olson, and plenty more are still around. Meanwhile, Atlanta will send out one of their Trade Deadline acquisitions, Tyler Mahle, who will make his Braves debut.

It'll be a fun showdown … whenever they get to play it. The weather in the Bronx is crummy at the moment and even though first pitch is still an hour away, the Yankees have announced that the game will not begin at 7:05pm ET as expected. Whenever the Yanks and MLB offer updates, we'll update our own article in turn. Stay dry and hang in there! The rain is supposed to subside, so we should get baseball tonight.

Please be advised we do not intend to start tonight’s game on time. Information will be provided as it is received.

Tonight’s first pitch is scheduled for approximately 9:00 PM.

Well, it took awhile, but we finally got an update. We'll see you in a little over 45 minutes for first pitch from Fried at 9pm ET.

fullText:
As the Atlanta Braves go for their ninth straight win on Friday evening against the New York Yankees, a piece of news dropped across MLB about a recent Braves pitcher who spent three seasons in the organization.

Following being let go by the Kansas City Royals, pitcher Aaron Bummer is officially an MLB free agent again for any organization to sign.

GettyDENVER, COLORADO – AUGUST 2: Aaron Bummer #36 of the Kansas City Royals pitches in the sixth innning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field on August 2, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images)

A few days ago, the Kansas City Royals designated Aaron Bummer for assignment.

Bummer, 32, was sent outright to AAA Omaha, but he rejected that assignment and departed the organization in favor of MLB free agency.

With the Royals, Aaron Bummer pitched just 1.1 innings and allowed 6 earned runs in the process, which makes it obvious why he was let go.

Aaron Bummer also pitched with the Atlanta Braves this season and wasn't very effective in his appearances either, posting an ERA of 10.26 across 16+ innings with 19 earned runs allowed and just 13 strikeouts.

The Braves likely aren't in favor of bringing back Aaron Bummer, and he may contemplate retirement after putting together a less-than-ideal 2026 campaign from a stats perspective.

CBSSports' RotoWire staff wrote (about his free agency decision):

"The veteran left-hander had his contract selected last weekend, and he pitched in two games out of the bullpen for Kansas City. Bummer faced 11 batters but recorded just four outs, allowing six runs on six hits and one walk with no strikeouts. He'll try to find work elsewhere rather than heading to Omaha."

More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Make Matt Olson Change Amid Yankees Series

GettyPHOENIX, ARIZONA – APRIL 25: Relief pitcher Aaron Bummer #49 of the Atlanta Braves pitches against the Arizona Diamondbacks during the MLB game at Chase Field on April 25, 2025 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images)

A very unproductive 2026 season will overshadow a relatively solid three-year stint with the Braves for Aaron Bummer.

He joined the club in 2024 after spending seven seasons with the Chicago White Sox.

In 2024, he posted a 3.58 ERA with Atlanta over 55+ innings with 69 strikeouts.

fullText:
NEW YORK — It sounds like Carlos Rodón will rejoin the Yankees' rotation soon.

The southpaw, out with elbow inflammation since June 30, is scheduled to make his first rehab start at Triple-A on Saturday. The plan is for Rodón to throw close to 50 pitches for the RailRiders.

From there, Rodón may or may not make one more rehab start, manager Aaron Boone said Friday. Either way, the Yankees will activate the pitcher before he's fully built up and "definitely probably piggyback him" in his initial starts, Boone said.

With a number of off days on the upcoming schedule and five healthy starters already in their rotation, the Yankees should be able to make that strategy work without taxing their bullpen. The long-held assumption has been that the Bombers will move Ryan Weathers or Will Warren to the pen anyway once Rodón returns, so either could be the piggyback pitcher while staying stretched out in this scenario.

Rodón, 33, went 4-2 with a 3.30 ERA over nine starts before going back on the IL.

He initially hoped to miss minimal time due to the inflammation, but he's been out over a month now. He said that multiple rounds of shots — he's gotten PRP and orthovisc injections — are to blame for the prolonged timeline.

"I always try to get back as quick as I can," Rodón said Friday. "I feel like anybody in this situation would. I wouldn't say anything delayed me. We just had a plan with the injections, and when you're scheduling injections and trying to throw in between them, it kind of makes it harder to figure out when you can throw, when you can't. Because when you get an injection, you might need a day off. Obviously, you take the first day off. You might need a couple more days.

So obviously, I would love to be pitching for our team right now. But right now, it's just building pitch count and getting in games, and that's it."

A look at Wells’ catcher’s equipment brought many raised eyebrows, because it did not have the modern appearance of so many at the position in the 2025 season. Munson was the captain of the Yankees and played a key role on the World Series championship teams of 1977 and ’78. More than the numbers, Munson is remembered for the fire he had behind the plate and his willingness to lead the Yankees into battle. He was always willing to block the plate and take the abuse of a runner crashing into him if it meant preventing a run from scoring.

He is remembered today as one of the team’s legends, and Wells was not about to let the anniversary of his death go without his tribute.

title: The 'greatest in the world' with an Olympic dream for Team GB
description: Jazz Chisholm Jr's New York Yankees' team-mates tell him regularly just how good he is - but will Team GB get the benefit?
fullText:
He's a Major League Baseball star who could be in line to represent Team GB at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

And Jazz Chisholm Jr's New York Yankees team-mates tell him regularly just how good he is.

"Sometimes they've seen me dragging a little bit lately," he said in a post-match interview last month. "So they've been saying: 'Let's not forget who you are. You're the greatest in the world... you are Jazz Chisholm.'"

Chisholm exudes a self-confidence that has endeared him to Yankees fans well versed in big personalities and supportive of those who embrace their huge expectations.

Just this week he made headlines for a video in which he was asked to stay silent until he heard the name of a better player than himself.

He didn't say a word - even when the reporter mentioned team-mate Aaron Judge, who is widely regarded as one of the greatest Yankees ever.

But behind the sometimes brash front, there is a humble side to Chisholm.

Born in Nassau - the capital city of the Bahamas - Chisholm was raised mainly by his grandparents.

His maternal grandmother - Patricia Coakley - had been the star player of the nation's softball team. She began teaching her grandson how to hit a baseball from the age of two, and encouraged him to play with swagger and flair.

His paternal grandmother - Judy Chisholm - also played a vital role in keeping his baseball ambitions on track.

When Jazz was 12, he moved to Wichita in Kansas to attend boarding school - the best route to give himself a chance of becoming a professional athlete.

He soon became severely homesick and wanted to go home but Judy convinced him to tough it out.

After graduating and returning to the Bahamas, he was signed by the Arizona Diamondbacks through the international scouting process.

Bahamians are eligible to play for Great Britain in the World Baseball Classic - an international competition that is the closest thing the sport has to a World Cup.

Chisholm was part of the squad for this year's tournament in March - just weeks before the MLB season - and did not disappoint, captaining the team and batting in three runs in an 8-1 defeat of Brazil.

He has made no secret of his desire to represent Britain at the Olympics, but there are several hurdles to overcome.

First, the team have to qualify.

Only one European nation can book their spot in LA when qualifying takes place next year. The competition is open, but GB would probably have to go further than Italy, who unexpectedly beat the USA in reaching the semi-finals of the World Baseball Classic.

Then there are the eligibility criteria. Only athletes who are legally British citizens can compete for Team GB at the Olympics, so Chisholm would have to apply for a British passport.

The final sticking point is the Olympics fall right in the middle of the MLB season, so an agreement still needs to be reached to release players.

An 11-day mid-season break is the latest proposal that may suit all sides as the MLB aims to minimise disruption to its season and the International Olympic Committee looks to ensure it is able to showcase the game's best players.

"I think when you see an Olympic competition, you expect to see best on best," IOC sports director Pierre Ducrey told the BBC.

"That's what we delivered, for example, in ice hockey in Milan-Cortina with the return of the National Hockey League, and we hope we can see that materialising in LA.

"Baseball is a sport proposed by LA28, so they are leading those conversations but we, of course, support as much as we can with the hope that come 2028, we're going to see the best of the best going at it in the Dodgers Stadium."

Watch MLB Bases Covered Live: New York Yankees @ Chicago Cubs

For Chisholm, the Olympics can wait for now - because the immediate goal is to help the Yankees in their quest to secure a 28th World Series title.

The next step on that journey is a three-match series against the Chicago Cubs, with the final game live on the BBC from 19:10 BST on Sunday.

The Yankees haven't won the big prize since 2009, making this their longest run without the title since 1920.

They fell agonisingly short last season - losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in the deciding game of the seven-game World Series - but are on course to reach the post-season again in 2026.

That gives Chisholm a route to living up to the tag he has been given to his team-mates - help the Yankees secure that long-awaited title.

title: Cody Bellinger injury adds urgency to Yankees trade deadline plans
description: Cody Bellinger's Grade 2 hamstring strain adds pressure on the Yankees to upgrade before the MLB trade deadline.
fullText:
Cody Bellinger’s worse-than-expected hamstring strain adds a new layer to the Yankees’ trade deadline period.

Diagnosed on Monday with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain, Bellinger’s four-to-six week timeline to return puts him back in the Yankees’ lineup sometime in September.

But even with Bellinger, a compromised Yankees lineup – no Aaron Judge since June 2, no Giancarlo Stanton since April 25 – had become a deeper issue.

Before their 9-5 win against the White Sox on Monday night, the second-place Yankees were 14-19 since June 19, averaging 3.27 runs per game.

Prior to that, the Yankees were averaging 5.27 runs per game and leading the AL East by 3.5 games.

Of course, every pinstriped hope of a deep October run is connected to Judge’s return.

And we’re still waiting on the second re-imaging of Judge’s fractured first right rib, and for his clearance just to begin baseball activity.

With Stanton, the constant he’s-getting-closer narrative should never limit the pursuit of more offense.

Still, impact bats are tough to find in this trade market, and you wonder about the appeal for the Yanks to absorb a bad contract or another DH-only type.

In recent days, potential offensive targets in Cincinnati’s Spencer Steer (wrist), San Francisco’s Casey Schmitt (knee) and even A’s catcher Shea Langeliers (knee), a longshot trade candidate, have receded due to injury.

A right-handed hitting outfielder is a better Yankee fit, and Kansas City has two impending free agents in Starling Marte and Lane Thomas. And the Mets' Tyrone Taylor is an increasingly intriguing option.

Elsewhere, if the Tigers choose to trade lefty ace Tarik Skubal, might they also be inclined to deal fellow impending free agent Gleyber Torres?

But the defensive fit in the Bronx is an issue, which also applies to Padres’ lefty-hitting second baseman Luis Arraez, also in his free agent walk year.

Still, the Bellinger situation doesn’t alter the Yanks’ top areas to upgrade.

The search for a swing-and-miss reliever and a right-handed hitting catcher could take the Yankees right up to Monday’s MLB trade deadline.

With an .856 OPS in nine games since his return from a left hamate bone fracture, right-handed hitting Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers – an impending free agent – is one possible target.

But the Twins are also three games back in the middling AL Central and one game behind for the last AL wild card spot entering Tuesday, so Jeffers’ trade status remains an interesting case.

And if there’s one huge trade to be made this deadline period, San Diego closer Mason Miller is the all-in candidate, with monumental end-game impact and team control through 2029.

If the Padres are inclined, lefty reliever Adrian Morejon – a free agent after this season – is a solid trade candidate. Plus, the Yanks’ past solid relationships with Luke Weaver and the rehabbing Clay Holmes (leg fracture) puts the Mets in play as a potential trade partner.

Bellinger’s absence further weakens the Yankees defensively, an overall area that needs to be addressed.

With appreciation of his utility value, Max Schuemann is an infielder playing out of position in left field, where Bellinger’s 19 defensive runs saved this year has boosted one of the league’s best pitching staffs.

For all his hard work and leadership, Amed Rosario is a liability at any defensive position, and he’s been less of a lefty masher this year, batting .197 overall in his last 25 games.

Top Yankees’ prospect George Lombard Jr. has initially struggled to hit each time he’s moved up a level, and you’d be asking a lot for him to debut in a pennant race.

But his plus-defensive skills at shortstop make him a prime candidate for an August call-up, as one more way to bolster the club’s pitching – its primary strength.

At last year’s deadline, the Yankees became a much better team down the stretch, in part, because of third baseman Ryan McMahon’s defensive presence.

Lombard could have that kind of impact even if he bats .208, which was McMahon’s average in 54 games after his arrival last summer from Colorado.

Realmuto each singling, but facing Angel Chivilli, Bryson Stott popped out into foul territory to end the threat. title: Yankees potential trade target: Reid Detmers
description: Should the Yankees be in play on the second-best lefty on the market?
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels are a mess, and are likely best served by opening the floodgates this trade deadline. They leaked on Thursday that they are interested in trading shortstop Zack Neto, but perhaps the single most-likely-to-be-dealt player on the entire market is lefty starter Reid Detmers.

Detmers just turned 27 and is under team control for two seasons after this. He’s always been decent enough, with a pair of two-win seasons and a strong bullpen year in 2025 that was cut short by elbow injury. This year, it’s a bit of a coming out campaign for Detmers, with a 3.27 FIP and 3.32 xERA contributing to a 3.0 fWAR across 120 innings so far in 2026.

If he played for a functioning franchise, he’d probably be approached with an extension — 3.5-4 win seasons from guys in their age-27 seasons are nothing to sneeze at. But this isn’t a functioning franchise, and the returns from dealing away a player like this are probably 

Detmers features one of the best arrays of breaking pitches in the sport, especially his slider, which he’ll often front door against southpaws and run hard away from right handed batters. It’s been a +14 (!!) run pitch for him this year, running a 35 percent whiff rate. His curveball, which has seen usage drop off this year, gets a whiff 38 percent of the time, and you wonder if the right idea is to lean into pitching backwards even more. Neither of his four-seam nor sinking fastball are all that good, and that may be what keeps him outside the inner circle of elite starters. Then again, the Yankees have had success developing all kinds of fastballs making him the kind of pitcher that fits Matt Blake’s pitching lab — play up the breaking balls that are working, and add some shape to a fastball while in a rotation that features some damn good heaters.

The added benefit of trading for Detmers is that you also functionally trade for a reliever at the same time. We’ve batted around all year which guy in the rotation is best suited to shore up a bullpen that desperately needs some reinforcement, and landing Detmers, who would be a better option than both Ryan Weathers and Will Warren, in my opinion lets you transfer one of those two to the relief corps. Even if you don’t want to do that, you give the rotation margin for rest. You may want to give Max Fried or Gerrit Cole the odd day off, or save Cam Schlittler’s arm in a random September start and hope that helps him in the postseason, and an additional very good pitcher gets you that room to breathe.

The downside is cost. Detmers’ skill and team control means he’s going to be pricey, and you almost drool at the potential he could reach in a pitching lab like the Brewers’. title: Cam Schlittler strikes out 12 in Yankees win over Phillies, 1-0
description: Yankees star Cam Schlittler struck out 12 Phillies batters through 7.1 innings pitched as New York emerged 1-0 victors.
fullText:
The Yankees (58-45) beat the Philadelphia Phillies (56-48) in their road series opener on Friday night, 1-0, the final score.

-- Yankees first baseman Paul Goldschmidt opened the scoring with an opposite-field line drive solo homer, recording the team's first hit of the game in the fourth inning against Phillies southpaw Jesús Luzardo.

-- Yankees starting pitcher Cam Schlittler also allowed his first hit in the fourth inning, a double by Phillies slugger Kyle Schwarber with one out. Schlittler battled back to retire the next two batters and strand the runner in scoring position.

-- Goldschmidt came to the plate with the bases loaded and two outs in the fifth, but he softly grounded out and the score remained 1-0 Yanks.

-- Luzardo tossed seven innings, holding the Yankees to just one run, allowing three hits and one walk while striking out nine batters.

-- Not to be outdone by his counterpart, Schlittler was utterly dominant on the hill. He struck out every member of the Phillies batting order apart from Schwarber, racking up 12 strikeouts in the process. He finally slipped up with one man out in the eighth inning, allowing a single to J.T. Realmuto before promptly hitting Gabriel Rincones Jr. with a pitch. Schlittler was pulled having completed 7.1 innings, allowing three hits, walking zero batters, and throwing 99 pitches. Stalwart lefty Brent Headrick emerged from the bullpen to relieve the Yankee starter.

-- Edmundo Sosa roped a single into right field to load the bases on Headrick. After a lengthy battle, Trea Turner lined out to left field, but not deep enough to score Realmuto on a sacrifice. With two outs, Schwarber worked the count to 3-2, but Headrick got out of the jam with a groundout and held New York's one-run lead entering the ninth inning.

-- Lefty reliever José Alvarado plunked Ryan McMahon (who was pinch-hitting for Amed Rosario), but recovered by forcing Cody Bellinger into a groundout double play, holding the Yankees scoreless in the top half of the final frame.

-- David Bednar entered the 1-0 ballgame to face the heart of Philadelphia's order. Bednar struck out Bryce Harper swinging, got some assistance from Bellinger's leaping catch near the left-field wall for the second out, and got Alec Bohm to ground out to end the game. Bednar earned his 19th save of the season, and Schlittler earned his 10th win.

Among all American League pitchers who have accumulated at least 75 IP, Schlittler's 2026 ERA (2.07) is tops, and he's second-best in WHIP (0.93) behind Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal.

title: Yankees Make Spencer Jones Roster Move Before Trade Deadline
description: The New York Yankees have quietly moved their top-ranked prospect outfielder following trade reports.
fullText:
The New York Yankees entered the final stretch before the MLB trade deadline with one of baseball's deepest farm systems and a front office facing difficult decisions. As the club continues weighing whether to move top prospects in pursuit of another postseason run, one of its most recognizable young players has remained at the center of speculation.

Hulking outfielder Spencer Jones has long been viewed as a cornerstone prospect thanks to his rare combination of size, athleticism and power. But after multiple trips between Triple-A and the majors this season, his future in the organization has become a popular topic as rival executives search for impact young talent and the Yankees look to upgrade other areas of the roster before the trade deadline.

FORBES | By Peter Chawaga
Cubs’ Craig Counsell Sends Front Office Message Shortly Before Trade Deadline

Industry chatter intensified this week when Jones' name surfaced in reports discussing the Yankees' deadline strategy.

"Spencer Jones and Jasson Dominguez are two of the key pieces the Yankees are planning to use as trade assets ahead of the Trade Deadline, according to industry sources,” MLB insider Francys Romero reported on X.

Whether New York ultimately parts with either of those promising young outfielders remains to be seen, but the report immediately fueled discussion surrounding Jones' place in the organization's long-term plans.

And that speculation gained another layer on Thursday, when the Yankees made another roster move involving the 24-year-old outfielder, moving him back down to their Triple-A affiliate just a few hours after calling him up to the big-league roster, according to the official transaction log.

FORBES | By Peter Chawaga
Trump Picks Replacement For Mets’ Steve Cohen Amid Historic Losing

Jones' latest demotion follows a very brief and unheralded opportunity to establish himself at the major league level, suggesting he might be falling out of favor in the Bronx.

“Spencer Jones made his big-league debut to great fanfare on May 8 in Milwaukee, having been called up from the minors when Jasson Dominguez landed on the injured list,” Erik Boland reported for Newsday. “Jones, considered a can't-miss Yankees prospect, much in the way Dominguez was at one point, was recalled to the majors for Wednesday's doubleheader against the (Pittsburgh) Pirates to significantly less fanfare. And this time around, his stay in the big leagues, his third stint this season, was assured to be a brief one.”

Indeed, the stint lasted less than 24 hours.

Through 31 major league games this season, Jones is batting just .224 with two home runs and a .669 OPS. His strikeout rate has remained a significant obstacle, with 35 strikeouts in only 76 at-bats.

For now, the Yankees appear focused on giving Jones additional at-bats in Triple-A while simultaneously evaluating their deadline options. Whether he returns to the Bronx later this season or becomes part of a blockbuster deal could be one of the organization's biggest storylines before the trade deadline passes.

The New York Yankees are reportedly “set to sign Sebastian Perez for a $1.7 million signing bonus in the 2027 international drafting class,” states MLB International Reporter Wilber Sanchez, but Francys Romero was the first to report this news back in February. It was also mentioned by Sanchez in February that Perez originally had a deal in place with the Pittsburgh Pirates, but that the deal fell through, also adding that some scouts believe “he’s one of the best catchers in his draft class” and has lots of power and speed that could translate well to the big leagues one day, reported Sanchez.

MLB International Reporter Francys Romero was the first to report that the Yankees were the “expected team to sign Perez” to this deal, with Perez being a catcher out of Venezuela. Romero further added that at this time, back in February, the signing period doesn’t open until January 15th, 2027, and that this is considered to be “the first major agreement since the Yankees found a new international director of scouting”, stated Romero. Romero also added how Perez’s “original deal with the Pirates was for $1.3 million, but Perez’s representatives went back out on the market for a larger bonus deal”, reported Romero.

Romero has also described Perez’s scouting report as similar to Sanchez’s report today, noting that he hits for a lot of power (high exit velocity) and is an “excellent” defender behind the plate. Reporter Wilber Sanchez recently interviewed Perez to gather his thoughts. When discussing what it means to join the Yankees organization, Perez stated, “I feel good, I’m so excited to belong to the Yankees.” Perez even went on to add how he loved this organization growing up, and his goal is to make the Major Leagues within the next couple of years, Perez said.

The Yankees have changed their approach to international scouting and signing in recent months. The Yankees organization had “parted ways” with former director of scouting Danny Rowland, who had been the Yankees’ head director of international scouting for 15 seasons. Rowland signed international players such as Jasson Dominguez, Miguel Andujar, Luis Severino, and Roderick Arias, but there wasn’t a good track record of success in this department.

The Yankees felt it was best to go in a different direction, leading them to promote Mario Garza as the new director of international scouting this past offseason, a move that was officially announced on June 28th via a report from Yankees beat writer Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. Garza has been with the Yankees for up to 16 years and has reportedly worked in a variety of player development and coaching positions with the Yankees in their farm system, reported Hoch. The Yankees have taken a liking to Garza and his strategy as it relates to evaluating talent, as Hoch also reported Yankees General Manager Brian Cashman, when speaking about Garza, stated: “He knows our systems. He already knows all the personnel we want”, Cashman told Hoch.

The Yankees International Scouting Department has gotten to work recently. Not just with this reported deal expected in January, but also with the recent signing of Taiwanese pitcher Chien Fan Lai, who is fresh out of high school, has already reported to the Yankees Dominican Summer League Academy, and is currently in a throwing program. The Yankees’ overhaul in their international scouting department is a change they hope pays dividends 10-15 years down the line as new talent enters the Bronx in the foreseeable future.

fullText:

The Red Sox swept their two games against the Rays on Friday while the Pirates had an opportunity to do the same to the Guardians on Saturday to ratchet up the drama in the East and Central.

The Red Sox rode a seventh-inning comeback to take the first three games of this four game set from the first-place Rays, giving Boston a 12-game winning streak. Neither of the starting pitchers pulled their weight, Ian Seymour lasting just three innings for Tampa after allowing three runs on two hits and two walks while Patrick Sandoval allowed five runs (four earned) on nine hits and a walk in five innings.

The Rays opened the scoring in the second as Ryan Vilade led off with a double and scored on a Chandler Simpson single, the speedy left fielder then advancing to second on a throwing error and scoring on a Nick Fortes RBI single. Boston responded with a pair in the bottom-half, Andruw Monasterio drawing an ABS-assisted walk and scoring on a two-run homer from Jahmai Jones. They grabbed a lead the following inning on a solo shot from Wilyer Abreu, but Tampa answered with three in the fourth on a Simpson leadoff double, a Victor Mesa Jr. two-run blast, Richie Palacios double, and Yandy Díaz RBI single, though Díaz would be thrown out at the plate to end the inning on an ensuing double by Jonny DeLuca.

That out at home would prove the difference, as despite Tampa adding an insurance run on a solo shot from DeLuca in the seventh, Boston roared back with four runs in the bottom of that frame to grab the decisive lead. Monasterio led off with a double and advanced to third as Jarren Duran reached on a throwing error by Vilade to put runners on the corners with no outs. Masataka Yoshida brought Monasterio home with an RBI groundout and Ceddanne Rafaela plated Duran with an RBI double to draw within one. This brought Abreu to the plate to demolish his second home run of the game, this one a two-run shot to complete the comeback.

With the win, the Red Sox move above .500 for the first time since Opening Day. In the span of two weeks, they have gone from 15.5 games back in last place to third place and only seven games back of first.

Guardians rookie Travis Bazzana had himself quite the day. After tripling in his team’s only run in the early game, Bazzana won the nightcap with his first career walk-off home run. Pittsburgh scored the first three runs of the contest, one in each of the second, third, and fourth on a Brandon Lowe sac fly, Esmerlyn Valdez RBI double, and Jake Mangum RBI single. That lead held until the eighth when the Pirates bullpen imploded. Cleveland scored three in the eighth on singles by Steven Kwan, Brayan Rocchio, Chase DeLauter, and Kahlil Watson, aided by a pair of wild pitches. That set up the defining moment for Bazzana in the ninth. Patrick Bailey led off with a single but was thrown out at home on a Kwan double. However, Bazzana picked up his teammate with a two-run walk-off home run to draw the Guardians level with the White Sox atop the AL Central, Chicago remaining nominally ahead on winning percentage.

Toronto Blue Jays (46-52) 1, Chicago White Sox (51-46) 0

The Blue Jays suddenly find themselves in last place, so perhaps it is fitting that Shane Bieber pitched his best start of the year — six shutout innings allowing three hits and two walks against six strikeouts — just in time to be shopped at the Trade Deadline. The three relievers that followed kept the shutout intact, allowing just a hit and a walk in the final three frames. The lone run of the contest came in the fourth, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. reaching on a one-out double and scoring on a George Springer RBI single.

Texas Rangers (50-48) 7, Atlanta Braves (56-41) 6

The Rangers became the first team in the AL West to reach 50 wins with a nail-biter against the Braves. After Joc Pederson led off the game with a homer Atlanta jumped out to an early 4-1 lead, Eli White hitting a two-run homer, Drake Baldwin an RBI single, and Ozzie Albies a sac fly in the second. Texas cut that deficit to one courtesy of RBI singles by Wyatt Langford and Brandon Nimmo in the third, but a Michael Harris II leadoff homer in the bottom of the frame restored Atlanta’s two-run cushion. In the sixth, it was the Rangers’ turn to score four runs, the first pair on an Evan Carter two-run blast to tie the game, 5-5, and the second pair on a two-run single from Nimmo with the bases loaded. Mauricio Dubón cut the deficit to one with an RBI double seventh, but Texas would hold on from there for the 7-6 win.

Seattle Mariners (49-50) 4, San Francisco Giants (42-56) 3

The Guardians weren’t the only team to win it with the last swing of the game, the Mariners avenging last night’s shutout loss with an extra-innings walk-off win over the Giants. In a battle of staff aces having relatively down years neither pitcher came out on top, Logan Webb allowing three runs on two hits and a walk in 6.2 innings while Bryan Woo allowed three runs (two earned) on three hits and two walks in six innings. San Francisco scored the first three runs of the game, rookie Bryce Eldridge lining an RBI single in the third and Rafael Devers and Willy Adames crushing a pair of solo home runs in the sixth. Cole Young responded with a three-run homer in the seventh to send the game to extras. In the bottom of the tenth, a Colt Emerson sac bunt advanced the automatic runner to third, and after a J.P. Crawford walk, Julio Rodríguez hit a ball just deep enough to left to bring Victor Robles home as the game-winning run.

The New York Yankees bullpen has invoked trust issues with fans all season–but that’s no thanks to Paul Blackburn.

Blackburn, 32, is a veteran in The Show. He’s pitched for the Athletics, Mets, and now the Yankees.

In his 14-year career, he’s been an All-Star once (2022) and is pitching like one again.

The last time the right-hander was pitching this well was in Oakland with the then-Oakland A’s during 2022. At that time, he was a starter, and a consistent one at that.

In the latter years of his career, he’s transitioned to a bullpen role. This year, everything is coming together.

Blackburn has a 2.22 ERA through 48.2 innings, with two games started and one save. With an ERA+ of 193, he’s been quite possibly the Yankees’ most reliable arm.

His value stems not only from elite-level production but also from his flexibility. Blackburn can cover multiple innings at a time and has done so at a very high level.

Yankee fans are starting to notice his breakout season.

FiresideYankees: “Paul Blackburn has a 1.16 ERA and a 3.26 FIP in his last 20 appearances for the Yankees, making some MASSIVE improvements from 2025. Velocity: 92.6 MPH -> 94.2 MPH GB%: 43.8% -> 56.8% ERA: 6.23 -> 2.22.”

Joe Randazzo: “Paul Blackburn is pitching like the type of reliever the Yankees should look to acquire this deadline. If you had this on your bingo card, it’s safe to say you know ball. This is certainly something I didn’t expect, and, in all honesty, I was a bit of a hater, annoyed this club was carrying too many long relievers with him and Ryan Yarbrough.”

Brayan Hoch: “Carlos Rodon threw 37 pitches in the 4th inning and is at 87. Yankees had Paul Blackburn warming before Rodon escaped with a strikeout.”

Talkin’ Yanks: “Max Fried went down into the tunnel after the third inning. Matt Blake immediately called down to the bullpen and got Paul Blackburn warming up.”

The Yankees are currently trailing the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East by three games.

New York will return from the All-Star break with a huge series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

LA has been amongst MLB’s best teams for years, and is coming off back-to-back World Series championships.

It’ll be a huge test for the Yanks to start off their second half against the fearsome world champs.

With team captain Aaron Judge sidelined, it’ll be up to All-Star Game MVP Cody Bellinger and Home Run Derby participant Ben Rice to right the ship.

title: Yankees Predicted to Part Ways With $16 Million Infielder Amid Struggles
description: The New York Yankees could trade struggling third baseman Ryan McMahon, an MLB analyst suggested. The post Yankees Predicted to Part Ways With $16 Million Infielder Amid Struggles appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Yankees have some holes to fill before the upcoming MLB trade deadline, but they could also make some subtractions to shore up their lineup.

The Yankees have a dire need for steady hitting to make up for the injured Aaron Judge, especially among their catchers. The team has already been linked to some hot trade targets, though its not yet clear just how aggressive the team will be in filling those needs.

The Yankees could do some strategic selling as well. Reporter Devon Platana of SI.com identified some Yankees players who could hit the trade block in the coming weeks, including an expensive infielder who has failed to produce much for the team.

Platana identified third baseman Ryan McMahon as one of the most likely trade pieces for the Yankees, along with shortstop Anthony Volpe. It could be more urgent for the Yankees to trade McMahon given the relatively large salary he carries.

“As mentioned earlier, the left side of the Yankees’ infield has left much to be desired,” Platana reported. “Volpe is only one half of the equation, though, as third baseman Ryan McMahon has been just as frustrating, if not more so, as he disappoints despite making $16 million annually.”

McMahon has struggled since joining the Yankees last season, hitting a low point this year as he is batting just .214 with a .655 OPS. Platana noted that his performance is “nothing short of underwhelming,” exacerbated by the fact that McMahon has the seventh-highest payroll on the team this season.

While he struggles at the plate, McMahon isn’t exactly offering relief on defense, Platana added.

“The Yankees should do whatever it takes to move on from McMahon and upgrade 3B, as he’s due to make another $16 million next season before becoming a free agent,” Platana wrote. “It’s better to turn the page now when, hopefully, a team will be desperate enough to roll the dice on the former All-Star, rather than losing him for nothing in 2027.”

Platana warned that the Yankees would not get much of a return for McMahon, but that shouldn’t hold them back from making a move if they find a willing trade partner.

“Even if a trade doesn’t yield the biggest return, trading McMahon away would be addition by subtraction, leaving Boone & Co. with one less headache to worry about,” Platana wrote.

McMahon could be used as a trade piece to help the Yankees land much-needed help elsewhere on the roster. MLB.com broke down the trade needs for each team, noting that the Yankees are in dire need of a catcher who can swing the bat.

“Entering the break, Yankees catchers ranked near the bottom of the league with a .176 batting average, .552 OPS and 46 wRC+,” the report noted. “While there are concerns about importing a catcher in-season because of potential disruption to the pitching staff, the Yankees have been strongly connected to the Twins’ Ryan Jeffers, who could comprise the right-handed-hitting part of a platoon with Austin Wells.”

fullText:
WASHINGTON — With a dazzling first half in the books, Cam Schlittler’s next stop could be the mound at Citizens Bank Park.

The first-time All-Star put the finishing touches on his case to start the Midsummer Classic for the American League on Saturday, allowing two earned runs over 6 2/3 innings in a 4-2 win over the Nationals. While Schlittler surrendered home runs to James Wood and Curtis Mead in the opening inning, the Yankees pulled off a late comeback for the second straight game when Ryan McMahon, Trent Grisham and Paul Goldschmidt all homered in the eighth inning.

McMahon and Goldschmidt slugged solo shots, while Grisham’s in-between, go-ahead blast put two runs on the board. With that, a Yankees team that had previously lost 15 of 20 pulled off its third straight win.

“It’s electric to come back,” Schlittler said. “They bailed me out a little bit.”

But Schlittler did his part, providing coverage for a taxed bullpen and limiting a high-octane offense. The Nationals made for a particularly tough matchup, as they entered the game fourth in average (.274) and first in slugging (.481) against fastballs. Schlittler, meanwhile, throws a fastball variant — he has a four-seamer, cutter and sinker — 91.5% of the time.

While Wood and Mead smoked some heaters, Schlittler was able to improve his execution and command as the game went on.

“That’s a heavy offense that they run at you,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said, “so it’s certainly a test, that’s for sure.”

With another passing grade, Schlittler now has a 2.05 ERA, the best among American League starters. His 3.6 fWAR ranked second in the league to Toronto’s Dylan Cease (3.7) prior to Saturday’s start.

Schlittler, who made his MLB debut on July 9 last season, has also recorded 137 strikeouts and 25 walks over 118 2/3 innings after totaling six strikeouts and an uncharacteristic four free passes on Saturday.

“What he’s done all year is just really special,” said David Bednar, who got the save on Saturday after throwing two innings on Friday. “He showcased that today.”

Prior to the victory, Boone said that “there’s a good chance” that Schlittler will pitch in Tuesday’s All-Star Game. However, he and Schlittler wanted to make sure that the right-hander got through his final start of the half without incident before making any commitments. Boone added that he had yet to hear from Blue Jays skipper John Schneider, who is managing the AL squad, about Schlittler’s potential usage.

While Schneider could tab his own guy to start, Schlittler has better numbers than Cease, who has already said that the pinstriper has “earned” the right, per MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson.

“We really just haven’t had that conversation yet,” Schlittler said. “We’ll see what happens in the next day or two, and if I’m comfortable doing that, then I’ll do that.”

Getting Schlittler into the star-studded exhibition shouldn’t be an issue. Tuesday lines up as a throw day — Schlittler would typically have a bullpen session — for the emerging ace. While a few nationally televised at-bats against some of baseball’s elites would come with more intensity, the scheduling should also give Schlittler enough time to recover and start Friday’s series-opener against the reigning champion Dodgers if the Yankees wish to go that route.

Either way, the 25-year-old is looking forward to the All-Star festivities in Philadelphia. Schlittler has volunteered to be Ben Rice’s “Gatorade guy” in Monday’s Home Run Derby, and his parents, siblings, grandma and uncle are attending the annual gathering of baseball’s top talent, of which he is now decidedly a part of.

“It’d be a cool experience,” Schlittler said of pitching in the game. “Not gonna lie, I’m not too worried about it. I got more things to worry about in terms of just this team and how we’ve been playing, and I like how it’s been the last couple days.

“It’d be good to end on a good note, get that sweep, go to Philly and just be comfortable with that.”

title: Yankees Draft: Everything you need to know to follow the 2026 edition
description: The MLB Draft begins this afternoon! Here’s how to track the results.
fullText:
It’s that special time of year again. A new generation of Yankees will enter the farm system in the coming days and weeks through the Major League Baseball Draft, seeking to make their mark on this historic franchise. The highest picks will understandably get the most attention, but remember that impact can come from anywhere. Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice have Cy Young and MVP cases this year while making their first All-Star Game, and the Yankees nabbed them in the seventh and 12th round of the 2022 and 2021 drafts, respectively.

Jake, Madison, Michael, Peter, Jonathan, and our old friend Dan Kelly—who previewed the draft for us—will join me in delving into all of the Yankees’ new draft picks, from their first four today to Round 5 and beyond tomorrow. Note that the two-day draft schedule from Philadelphia is a little different from last year and very different from the years before that, when this was a three-day event. If you’re curious about who the Yankees might take, Dan wrote a good roundup of names from recent mock drafts, though as he notes, predicting who exactly will still be on the board at No. 35 overall is quite difficult.

If you have any interest in following the MLB Draft proceedings beyond PSA’s coverage (which you can find here), check out the viewing guide below. The best guess is that the Yankees won’t pick until around 4pm-ish.

1:00-2:30 p.m. ET – Preview show + Picks 1-10 (NBC/Peacock)
2:30-4:30 p.m. ET – Picks 11-40 (MLB Network, MLB.com, MLB.tv, MLB+)
4:30-7:45 p.m. ET – Picks 41-135 (MLB.com, MLB.tv, MLB+)

11:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. ET (MLB.com, MLB.TV, MLB+)

Below is the draft order for Sunday’s coverage. The Yankees are picking 10 spots behind where they would have lined up due to luxury tax penalties (as are the Dodgers, Mets, Phillies, and Blue Jays). So their first pick won’t come until No. 35 overall, though because they didn’t sign any free agents this past offseason, they do have all their expected picks.

Note that under current MLB rules, the only draft picks that can be traded are Competitive Balance Round picks, and while the Yankees are technically picking in the first Competitive Balance Round, it is considered an untradeable first-round pick that simply moved back 10 spots.

The first half of the first round was primarily curated by last December’s MLB Draft Lottery, which the White Sox won. The Rays are in first place right now, but they fared well in the lotto last year and will get the No.2 pick, with the Twins selecting after them. UCLA shortstop Roch Cholowsky, Georgia Tech catcher Vahn Lackey, and Texas high school shortstop Grady Emerson are all expected to go within the first three picks, though it remains to be seen who the Pale Hose will pick to kick off the action. As a darkly amusing reminder (like with the White Sox from 2024-25), the 119-loss Rockies were ineligible from picking any higher than 10th this year because they’re a revenue sharing team that also had lotto picks in 2024 and 2025.

That’s enough semantics. Here’s the order!

Prospect Promotion Incentive Picks

Braves [for Drake Baldwin winning NL Rookie of the Year]

Mets [No. 17 pick moved back due to luxury tax]

Astros [for Hunter Brown finishing in the top three for AL Cy Young]

Giants [acquired from Guardians for Patrick Bailey]

White Sox [acquired from Pirates for Jacob Gonzalez and Brandon Eisert]

Yankees [No. 25 pick moved back due to luxury tax]

Phillies [No. 26 pick moved back due to luxury tax]

Blue Jays [No. 29 pick moved back due to luxury tax]

Dodgers [No. 30 pick moved back due to luxury tax]

Pirates [compensation for unsigned 2025 No. 50 pick]

Competitive Balance/Compensation Round

Red Sox [acquired from Brewers for Caleb Durbin and two others)

Cardinals [acquired from Mariners for Brendan Donovan]

Cardinals [acquired from Rays in Brendan Donovan trade]

Cubs [for losing Kyle Tucker in free agency, and no luxury tax]

The draft will then be on hold until Sunday at 11:30am ET, and it will be a primarily MLB.com-focused event from there. Usually, they make it pretty easy to follow the draft picks though, and there won’t be much pomp and circumstance between selections. If anything, it will be just enough time for their draft experts to opine on the picks, and then it’s onto the next!

The draft order is largely the same in the fifth and sixth round, aside from the Dodgers losing picks due to various free agent signings. Then from the seventh round onward, it’s all straightforward “worst record to best record + playoff results” 1-30. You can check out the full order here.

Per Baseball America, the Yankees have a total draft bonus pool of $7,342,800 to spend (the lowest of all 30 teams), meaning that they can go over or under the given slot number on any pick, but in the end, their grand total must stay below that amount. Here’s how the slots are divvied up:

The Yankees can vary their bonus levels; any left over might be used to help sign draft prospects with signability questions in the 11th round and beyond for more than the allotted $150,000 value. Teams can spend over their allotted pools, but not without penalties:

A team that exceeds its bonus pool faces a penalty. A club outspending its allotment by 0-5 percent pays a 75 percent tax on the overage. At higher thresholds, a team loses future picks: a first-rounder and a 75 percent tax for surpassing its pool by more than 5 and up to 10 percent; a first- and a second-rounder and a 100 percent tax for more than 10 and up to 15 percent; and two first-rounders and a 100 percent tax for more than 15 percent.

title: Yankees at Nationals: 5 things to watch and series predictions | July 10-12
description: Here are five things to watch and predictions as the Yankees take on the Nationals in Washington D.C. for a three-game series starting Friday.
fullText:
Here are five things to watch and predictions as the Yankees hit the road to take on the Nationals in a three-game series starting Friday...

Wednesday's win over the Rays was huge -- not only did it prevent Tampa from clinching the tiebreaker for the AL East crown, the Yankees offense finally woke up from its slumber, scoring 12 runs.

They'll need to keep that momentum going this weekend so they can end the unofficial first half of the season on a good note. Winning the series against an up-and-coming Nationals team will go a long way to alleviating the pain the Yankees were in when they went 5-15 the last few weeks.

It won't be easy, but going into the All-Star break with a few wins over the weekend would go a long way.

Cam Schlittler is scheduled to make one more start (Saturday) before his first All-Star Game.

Of course, the regular season is more important than the Midsummer Classic, but the Yankees and Schlittler have been pretty mum about how they plan to approach this weekend and whether he'll pitch at all on Tuesday. If Schlittler mows down his opponent and is pitch-efficient, there's a good chance he'll toe the rubber in Philadelphia.

The Yanks may not wait until then to announce if Schlittler will pitch, but we can glean a lot from his start Saturday.

Oh, also, Schlittler returned to form with a masterful performance against the Rays earlier in the week, bouncing back from a subpar performance. Schlittler took any negative comments about his "downfall" personally, and he can stick it to those people again this weekend.

The Yankees were so deep in their rotation with Ryan Weathers and Will Warren pulling their weight early on, but their last few times out have not given the team a shot.

Weathers (3-7, 4.29 ERA) has allowed six earned runs in his last 5.2 innings pitched (two starts).

Warren (7-4, 4.15 ERA) has been so inconsistent and laid a complete egg, allowing six runs in four innings against the Rays on Tuesday.

Max Fried will return and there's always the possibility the Yanks deal for another starter at the deadline, so both Weathers and Warren need to show they can contribute consistently unless their spots in the rotation will be taken.

The Nationals are having a solid season and are vying for a playoff spot in a competitive National League -- and they are doing it on the back of their offense.

Players like James Wood, CJ Abrams, Daylen Lile, and Luis Garcia Jr. have helped the Nationals become one of the best offenses in the majors. They are eighth in baseball in batting average (.251), tied with the Yankees for the most home runs (132), third in OPS (.760) and fourth in hits (809).

Yankees pitching will need to be careful with this lineup if they hope to come away with a series win.

Ben Rice has been one of the Yankees' best hitters, even when Aaron Judge was in the lineup. He was rewarded with his first All-Star Game selection and he will participate in the Home Run Derby. The slugging first baseman has been on a tear of late, smashing five homers in his last seven games.

He's ready for the derby, but can he continue that power surge this weekend?

Rice has been on a tear and is likely to continue that.

Schlittler will look to cement himself as the best AL pitcher before the All-Star break.

The outfielder is having a tremendous year, hitting .269 with 25 homers and 61 RBI as the Nats leadoff hitter.

Cole was charged with three runs over 6 1/3 innings. He gave up seven hits, struck out six and walked one on 97 pitches.

New York has lost 11 of its past 13 games.

Yankees manager Aaron Boone and bench coach Brad Ausmus were both ejected in the sixth inning.

The Yankees will start an opener against Rays RHP Drew Rasmussen (7-4, 2.78) on Thursday in the series finale.

title: Yankees Should Tade For Six-Time All-Star Closer At Trade Deadline
description: The New York Yankees are in a position to be buyers at this year's trade deadline
fullText:
The New York Yankees are in the middle of a rough stretch, but still have the second-most wins in the American League. They will clearly be looking to add at the trade deadline, and relievers may be on their shopping list.

The Yankees' bullpen is not bad by any means. Their 3.09 bullpen ERA is the second best in baseball, trailing only the Atlanta Braves. However, they could use a high-leverage arm. Camilo Doval has struggled since arriving in the Bronx and may not be reliable in big spots when the postseason begins. David Bednar has been solid as the closer, posting a 2.92 ERA and converting 17 of 19 save opportunities.

However, adding an elite closer could move Bednar into the setup role and allow Aaron Boone to deploy Doval, Brent Headrick and Fernando Cruz earlier in games. Josh Hader could be a player the Yankees target at the deadline.

Even though the Houston Astros are under .500 and on the outside looking in at the postseason, they are within striking distance of a postseason spot. They do not figure to be traditional sellers at the deadline, but could move Hader for the right price.
